style.vernacular: Danish colonial harbour town on steep hills: rubble-stone and ballast-brick two to three storey warehouses and townhouses in Georgian-derived Caribbean style, lime-washed or stuccoed in yellow, white and red with arched ground-floor arcades, shuttered openings and red or grey metal roofs, stepping up the hillsides in white and pastel concrete houses; modern resort and mall blocks in pastel render along the shore.
style.ornament: Georgian proportions with arched stone or brick ground-floor arcades, louvred green or white shutters, cast-iron or timber balconies and galleries, ballast-brick step streets, lime-washed rubblestone, pedimented fronts on churches, and cannons and chain fences left over from the harbour forts.

sources.what: largest collection of colonial buildings in the Caribbean, classic Caribbean adaptations of English Georgian built by the Danes in the 1830s; red walls of Fort Christian; step streets of ballast bricks; colonial warehouses in alleys turned into shops; three historic quarters
stone fort with diamond bastions, Victorian clock tower 1874
rubblestone walls, brick pillars, Greek Revival front with Gothic arched windows, hip roof
